jobs.title: Forensic Analyst - Entry to Mid Level (Maryland)
Forensics - Crisis and Investigations - Cyber Response - Manager

reading.body:
Two digital forensics openings were live in the federal data on October 3, 2026, both at US government agencies and both paying six figures at the top of their bands.

The pattern is narrow and public-sector. The National Security Agency in Fort Meade, Maryland and the US Postal Service in Richmond, California are the only two employers represented, and both roles sit in the same function. The salary ranges, $87,362 to $153,082 and $128,740 to $178,390, are wide enough to span entry through senior grades, which is what the titles say as well.

For AI specifically, this says little on its own. Digital forensics is adjacent to AI work rather than central to it, and two postings cannot establish a hiring trend in either direction. What the data does show is that the federal government is recruiting for investigative technical work at the same time it is standing up AI infrastructure, and that these roles are cleared, on-site positions at fixed facilities rather than remote listings.

What it does not tell the reader is volume. The page carries a count of two, drawn from a source list that includes aggregators and remote boards, so the absence of private-sector or remote forensics roles here reflects what was captured, not what exists. Nothing in this data speaks to compute, buildings, or power.

Two federal forensics postings is not a hiring signal, it is a sourcing signal. The source list behind this page includes aggregators and remote boards, yet both captured roles came from USAJobs, the one official government feed. That asymmetry suggests the pipeline is not measuring the forensics labor market, it is measuring which feeds return structured, verifiable listings. Private-sector forensics roles exist in quantity, but they route through company career boards and aggregators that either did not surface here or did not match the function tag.

The salary bands carry more information than the count. The NSA range spans $87,362 to $153,082, a spread of roughly $66,000 within a single posting. The Postal Service range spans $128,740 to $178,390, a spread of roughly $50,000. Bands that wide are grade ladders, not negotiated offers. They tell you the employer is hiring at multiple experience levels from one requisition, which is what a standing federal pipeline looks like rather than a targeted private-sector hire.

Both roles are tied to fixed facilities, Fort Meade and Richmond, and both sit inside agencies with their own compute and network infrastructure. That is the only thread connecting this page to the AI buildout, and it is a thread of adjacency, not causation. The data does not show whether either role touches AI systems, and it does not show what either agency is spending on compute.

What does the count of two actually measure?
It measures what the listed sources returned for this function on the build date of October 3, 2026. The source list includes USAJobs, Adzuna, Jooble, Remotive, Remote OK, Arbeitnow, The Muse, company career boards, Indeed Hiring Lab, and InfoSec Job Board. Both captured listings came from USAJobs, so the count reflects federal feed coverage rather than total market volume.

Why are both postings from government agencies?
The data shows only two employers, the National Security Agency and the US Postal Service, and both are federal. Nothing in the data explains why private-sector forensics employers are absent. The page cannot distinguish between a market with no private openings and a capture that missed them.

What do the salary ranges say about seniority?
The NSA role is titled entry to mid level and spans $87,362 to $153,082. The Postal Service role is titled senior and spans $128,740 to $178,390. The bands overlap, and both are wide enough to cover multiple grades, so the titles and the ranges are consistent with laddered federal pay scales rather than single-level offers.

Are any of these roles remote?
No. Both list fixed locations, Fort Meade, Maryland and Richmond, California. The source list includes Remotive and Remote OK, two remote boards, and neither produced a listing here. The data does not say whether remote forensics work exists, only that none was captured.

Do these jobs connect to AI infrastructure?
The data does not establish that. Neither posting description is included, only title, function, salary, employer, and location. Digital forensics is tagged as a security function, and nothing in the record links either role to compute, data centers, or power.

How current are these listings?
The NSA role was posted October 1, 2026, and the Postal Service role September 8, 2026. The page was built October 3, 2026, so both were live within the prior four weeks. The data does not include closing dates or application counts.
